claim_tested: BAG-1 links Hsc70/Hsp70 to the 26S proteasome through its own surface
key_finding: BAG-1 associates with the 26S proteasome in HeLa cells; binding is regulated by ATP hydrolysis and is not mediated by Hsc70/Hsp70; targeting BAG-1 to the proteasome brings the chaperones with it
context: human, HeLa cytosol, in vitro and in vivo
confidence_limits: high for human; no worm counterpart; does not localise the contact to a proteasome subunit

claim_tested: a ULD lysine is required for the proteasome-linked activity of BAG-1
key_finding: protection from stress-induced growth inhibition requires a conserved lysine in the BAG-1S ubiquitin-like domain thought to be important for proteasome binding, plus the C-terminal Hsc70-binding residues
context: human breast cancer cells, heat shock and other stresses
confidence_limits: phenotype is downstream of binding; the specific lysine is not identified in the abstract and needs curator verification against the paper

claim_tested: the ULD alone is the proteasome signal
key_finding: CHIP attaches a K11-linked atypical polyubiquitin chain to BAG-1 that does not cause degradation but stimulates proteasome association, and this requires the integrated ubiquitin-like domain at the same time
context: human, in vitro and in vivo
confidence_limits: implies a two-signal recognition; the worm has CHN-1 but BAG-1 is not a demonstrated CHN-1 substrate

claim_tested: where the BAG1 ULD binds the proteasome
key_finding: the BAG1 ULD sits on PSMD2/Rpn1 alone, burying 730 A^2 on the BAG1 side; all 16 interface residues lie in ULD 144-224; 58% of buried area comes from Ile44-patch-equivalent positions even though no canonical Ile44 patch exists
confidence_limits: 3.6 A limits side-chain placement; database-level until the primary paper is identified; human only

claim_tested: what worm BAG-1 and UNC-23 actually do
key_finding: C. elegans has exactly two BAG-domain proteins; UNC-23 C-terminal fragments stimulate HSC70 ATPase and regulate folding with lower affinity than BAG-1; unc-23 motility defects are cured by reducing the antagonistic cochaperone DNJ-13
context: C. elegans muscle, reporter strains and in vitro chaperone assays
confidence_limits: the only substantive worm biochemistry on this family; frames BAG-1 within the Hsc70 cycle, not the proteasome

claim_tested: whether worm chaperone-linked degradation needs a ULD shuttle
key_finding: CHN-1 and UFD-2 form an E3/E4 complex sufficient to multiubiquitylate UNC-45; chn-1 loss partially suppresses unc-45(ts)
confidence_limits: shows a worm chaperone-to-proteasome route that does not require BAG-1; does not exclude BAG-1

claim_tested: what the BAG-1 ULD does to client fate
key_finding: BAG-1 binds F508del-CFTR through its ubiquitin-like domain independently of Hsc70 and stabilises it, reducing ubiquitinylated CFTR, apparently by competing with ubiquitin
confidence_limits: the ULD can protect a client rather than deliver it; opposite sign to the seed hypothesis

claim_tested: whether BAG-1-driven degradation needs the ULD
key_finding: BAG1 promotes hERG degradation by shifting it to the TRC8 ligase; dissociation of the Hsp70/CHIP complex requires BAG1 binding to Hsp70 but does not involve the BAG1 ubiquitin-like domain
confidence_limits: explicitly separates a degradation-promoting BAG1 activity from the ULD

claim_tested: is the worm ULD surface compatible with the Rpn1 site
key_finding: worm ULD model superposes on the 9HEU BAG1 chain at TM 0.674, Calpha RMSD 3.42 A over 81 residues, and places 16 residues within 4.5 A of Rpn1 at the same positions as the human contacts, with 5 minor rigid-body clashes and no main-chain interpenetration
context: in silico, AlphaFold model of O44739 on a 3.6 A cryo-EM frame
confidence_limits: rigid placement without energetics or relaxation; proves absence of a steric barrier, not binding

claim_tested: how much of the interface depends on the positions named in the hypothesis
key_finding: the Arg72-equivalent Lys220, the one position where worm BAG-1 loses the chemical class (Gly81), buries 20.4 A^2, 2.8% of the BAG1 side; the five largest contributors (Arg214, Met216, Lys189, Ile218, Ile191) are all conserved in character in the worm
confidence_limits: buried area is not binding energy; two substantial divergences remain at Ser196 to Phe56 and Phe187 to Thr47, together 92 A^2

claim_tested: is the patch conserved across nematodes
key_finding: across 22 nematode BAG-1 orthologues the Ile44-equivalent is hydrophobic in 100% (Ile in only 14%), the Arg42-equivalent is Lys in 100%, the Lys48-equivalent is basic in 95%, the Val70-equivalent is M/L/I in 100%, and the Arg72-equivalent is Gly in 50% and Lys in 45%
confidence_limits: conservation at partly buried positions can reflect core packing; the Ile44-equivalent is only 16-22% solvent exposed in worm, human and ubiquitin alike

claim_tested: internal control: does the paralogue have the domain
key_finding: UNC-23 (O61980, 458 aa) has a BAG domain at 370-450 and a disordered N-terminal region 1-232 with no ubiquitin-like fold; its first 170 residues are unalignable to the BAG-1 ULD, so none of the patch positions exist
confidence_limits: confirms the control behaves as expected; any ULD-dependent property must be BAG-1 specific

claim_tested: is there worm evidence for BAG-1 at the proteasome
key_finding: searches for C. elegans bag-1 with proteasome, rpn-1 or interactome return no papers; the only PDB entry for O44739 is 1T7S (2.8 A, residues 74-210, BAG domain only), so the worm ULD has no experimental structure
confidence_limits: absence of evidence in indexed abstracts, not proof of absence
